subject: Controlled forged DNS transaction-ID response during guarded MCP fetch

environment.resolver: Ubuntu glibc 2.43; private netns resolv.conf search search-trap.test, ndots:5, timeout:1, attempts:1; no external route

attack.name: spoof-id.test
attack.payload: Plausible loopback A/AAAA answer with matching question and a transaction ID incremented modulo 65536; matching-ID answer is never sent
attack.expected: Resolver ignores forged answers; guarded_fetch returns EGRESS_DNS_FAILURE without transport socket

observed.direct_legacy_stdio: 2 mismatched private DNS responses ignored; EGRESS_DNS_FAILURE, no HTTP hit or returned body, approved GET recovered in the same process
observed.strace_legacy: 2 mismatched IDs; no extra AF_INET/AF_INET6 SOCK_STREAM socket after approved positive TCP control
observed.strace_modern: 2 mismatched IDs; no extra AF_INET/AF_INET6 SOCK_STREAM socket after approved positive TCP control

limitations: Finite local glibc resolver fixture; it does not prove all resolver implementations reject forged responses.
Raw strace traces were checked by the live harness but not retained; the compressed run log and source assertions are retained.
This direct stdio probe is not an installed native Codex/Claude/Cursor client replay. It does not cover host-client traffic or traffic sent through other tools.
No official candidate, owner residual-risk acceptance, or AI Scraping Defense repository gate is implied.
